en.title: Matrix Selection with Per-Row Limits
en.description:
Choose exactly x elements from an n×n matrix, with at most factor[i] from row i, to maximize the total. Output −1 if x elements cannot be chosen; output 0 when x=0.

The standard input format, examples and test data were written independently by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n x (1≤n≤1000, 0≤x≤n²); the second line contains n values factor (0..n); the next n lines contain the matrix, with values 1..10⁹.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: choose 8 and 6 from the first row, 10 from the second, and 5 and 1 from the third, which respects every row limit: 5 items with a total of 30. Example 2: the only row has limit 0, so the required 1 item cannot be chosen; output −1. Example 3: 0 items are required, and the empty selection sums to 0.
hints: Keep only the factor[i] largest elements of each row, then take the x largest among all candidates.
